task.goal: A build scheduler runs tasks with dependencies. It currently starts dependents as soon as their parent is started, may run a shared dependency twice, and never rejects cycles. Fix schedule(tasks, runner) in scheduler.py. Run each task once only after all dependencies have succeeded; preserve declaration order among ready tasks; stop on the first runner failure; raise ValueError for unknown dependencies or cycles before running any task. Run visible tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll inspect the scheduler and its tests first.Rewrote `schedule` in `scheduler.py`: `_validate` runs first and rejects unknown dependencies and cycles (including self-loops) with `ValueError` before any task runs; the execution loop then repeatedly picks the first declared task whose dependencies are all `done`, so each task runs exactly once, only after its parents, in declaration order, and a raising `runner` propagates immediately with no further tasks started.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest -v test_scheduler` passes (2 tests). Additional probes confirmed shared dependency runs once (`['shared', 'a', 'b']`), diamond order (`['base', 'mid1', 'mid2', 'top']`), unknown-dep and cycle rejection with zero runner calls, and failure stopping at the failing task. No limitations found for the stated requirements.
